resources.string: With it on, Coulomb can change a few settings of the phone and of single apps. Each change is shown before it runs, is logged with the value it replaced, and can be reverted. Nothing runs without your tap.
Turning it on also gives Coulomb the permission to write system settings (WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS).
Coulomb couldn’t save this setting. Free some storage and try again.
Coulomb’s helper process is not running, so nothing can be changed from here. Each action still shows its command, which you can run over adb.

plurals.name: actions_off_keep_body
plurals.item: %1$s change Coulomb made is still in force. You can revert it now or keep it; it stays in the log either way.
%1$s changes Coulomb made are still in force. You can revert them now or keep them; they stay in the log either way.

resources.string: Left still and unplugged, this phone can enter deep Doze %1$s after the screen goes off.
Coulomb couldn’t read the Doze settings.
The Doze setting holds a value Coulomb did not write: the phone’s maker or another tool set it. Coulomb leaves it alone until you take it over.
You took over the value found on %1$s. A profile keeps it and changes only what it needs.
Deep Doze about 30 min after the screen goes off
Deep Doze about 10 min after the screen goes off, and longer idle stretches
Limits background work and some effects until you turn it off or plug in.
Clears Android’s own battery history. It cannot be undone.
Actions for one app are on that app’s page, under Actions.
Android records this setting and does not act on it, so it would change nothing.
The only command for it cuts off every other app’s sensors instead.

plurals.name: actions_revert_all_body
plurals.item: %1$s change is put back. A value that something else changed since is left as it is.
%1$s changes are put back, newest first. A value that something else changed since is left as it is.

resources.string: Now %1$s. Coulomb leaves it as it is.
Stops the app now. It gets no alarms and shows no notifications until you open it again.
Stops the app’s work in the background. Its notifications can be late.
Android holds back the app’s jobs, alarms and network. Android moves it back as you use the app.
Android holds back the app’s jobs, alarms and network more than in any other bucket. Android moves it back as you use the app.
Lets the app run and use the network while the phone dozes. This costs battery.
The app waits for Doze like other apps. Its notifications can be late.
Changes how soon the phone enters deep Doze when it is left still. Background work and some notifications wait longer.
Coulomb records this value as the phone’s own and builds profiles on it. Nothing is written.
Android’s own battery statistics and history are cleared, for every app that reads them. Coulomb’s own records stay.
Revert it from the log, or run this command.
Nothing to undo: open the app and it runs again.
Stop managing it from the Action Center; the value stays.
This is the second and last question. Once cleared, Android’s statistics cannot be brought back.
Coulomb’s helper process is not running. You can run the command over adb.
Coulomb couldn’t read the current value, so it changes nothing.
Coulomb does not act on system apps, on itself or on the app that gives it access.
The app is not installed in this profile.
Something else set this app’s background mode. Coulomb changes it only from a plain “allowed”, so that it can put it back.
Android keeps this app’s bucket, or the app is already further out.
On the system’s own list, which no command changes.
Battery saver can’t change while the phone charges.
Take over the Doze setting first.
The Doze setting is not a list Coulomb can rewrite safely.
Nothing to change: this phone already enters deep Doze after %1$s.
Nothing to change: this phone already dozes sooner.
There is no outside value to take over.
Coulomb changed this already. Revert that change first.
Android set %1$s instead of what was asked. That is what the log holds.
The command ran and nothing changed.
The command ran, but Coulomb couldn’t read the result. The change is in the log.
Something else changed this value since, so Coulomb left it as it is.
The command failed and nothing was changed.
The Action Center is off, so Coulomb changes nothing about this app.
This app is in another profile. Coulomb acts only on apps of the profile it runs in.
